results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system, as recorded in VFB. VFB describes the mushroom body as divided into: the calyx, which is closest to the cortex and receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, which is a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes; and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages. VFB holds various data related to the mushroom body, including images, neurons with some part in the mushroom body, and parts of the mushroom body. For more detailed information, you can explore the available data in VFB, such as the [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of mushroom body") available images of mushroom body, [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in mushroom body, or [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") parts of mushroom body.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The types of Kenyon cells in the adult Drosophila brain include [[KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain")(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCab-c, [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [[Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open Kenyon cell of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), as well as alpha/beta Kenyon cell, alpha'/beta' Kenyon cell, and adult gamma Kenyon cell, which are further subdivided into subtypes such as core, surface, posterior, anterior-posterior, middle, and dorsal. This information comes from the VFB database, which lists [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of Kenyon cell. VFB holds a range of data on Kenyon cell, including [32328](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of Kenyon cell") images, scRNAseq data, transgene expression data, and connectivity data. For more specific information on the different types of Kenyon cells, you can explore the subclasses of Kenyon cell in VFB or examine the available scRNAseq data for Kenyon cell.

results.title: Basic connectivity
results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are sensory interneurons, as well as projection neurons from the antennal lobe. This information is based on data from VFB, which mentions that the calyx of the mushroom body receives sensory interneuron afferents. Additionally, VFB records show that larval antennal lobe multiglomerular projection neurons, such as C2, provide sensory interneuron afferents to the calyx. VFB holds a large number of records related to the mushroom body, including [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body, [366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, and [304](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPostsynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with postsynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with postsynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, which may be relevant for a narrower follow-up of the inputs to the mushroom body.

results.title: Cell count
results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response:

The connectome data indicates that there are approximately 9413 neurons with some part in this region. Additionally, VFB holds [462](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047887,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of adult central brain") records of parts of the adult central brain and [1](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047887,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in adult central brain") record of transgene expression in the adult central brain. 

Note that the EVIDENCE also mentions "more than 125,000 neurons" from VFB, but this figure is not specific to the adult central brain and its source is unclear. 

For an accurate biological total of neurons in the adult central brain, a published reference with a citation is required, which is not provided in the given EVIDENCE.

**Published neuron-count estimates — adult central brain** (from the literature):

- more than 125,000 neurons (adult Drosophila central brain connectome/model) — A Drosophila computational brain model reveals sensorimotor processing. — PMID 39358519
- ~139,255 neurons (whole adult Drosophila brain) — Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain. — PMID 39358518

_VFB has annotated 9,413 neuron types with some part in adult central brain — a curated annotation count, not the biological total._

results.title: Circuit motif
results.question: Describe the dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs). Which DAN types connect to which MBON types?
results.response:
The dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) comes from adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons, with dopamine release modifying the strength of Kenyon cell synapses to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) in the same region, as recorded in VFB. 

VFB holds a range of data on mushroom body output neurons, including [69](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of MBON") subclasses of MBON, single-cell RNA sequencing data for MBON, [158](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in MBON") records of transgene expression in MBON, [29859](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for MBON") downstream connectivity classes for MBON, and [23753](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for MBON") upstream connectivity classes for MBON. 

However, VFB does not currently hold specific data on which types of adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons connect to which types of MBONs.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The LPLC2 visual neuron type is a type of visual neuron with specific characteristics and functions. According to VFB, the cell body of LPLC2 lies in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind. It has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer, allowing it to detect looming stimuli. In the lobula, it has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4. The arbors of LPLC2 span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC2 cells. LPLC2 projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. Its activity elicits a jump escape response. VFB records show that there are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe and they are cholinergic. VFB does not currently hold comprehensive data on all connections of LPLC2, but the available information indicates that it has specific connections in the lobula and PVLP.

results.response: The organisation of the [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") in adult and larval Drosophila differs. According to VFB, both stages have glomerular organization, but the adult antennal lobe is more elaborated in terms of its glomerular neuropil. VFB also records that the organisation differs in terms of tract connections. VFB holds data on the comparison of region organization, which can be queried for more specific details on the differences between adult and larval antennal lobe organisation.

results.title: Publications for a circuit
results.question: What publications describe the PPL1 dopaminergic neurons and their role in aversive memory?
results.response: Publications describing the dopaminergic PPL1 neurons and their role in aversive memory include Claridge-Chang et al., 2009, Mao and Davis, 2009, Budnik and White, 1988, and Ren et al., 2016, as recorded in VFB. VFB holds information on the [dopaminergic PPL1 neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100219 "Open dopaminergic PPL1 neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), including its location in the posterior inferior lateral protocerebrum of the adult brain and its projections to various parts of the mushroom body. The connectome and neuron profile data in VFB indicate that the dopaminergic PPL1 neuron cell body is located in a cluster of approximately 12 cell bodies in the cortex of the posterior inferior lateral protocerebrum of the adult brain, immediately lateral to the mushroom body calyx. Furthermore, VFB contains records of publications that describe the role of dopaminergic PPL1 neurons in aversive memory, including titles such as 'Specific dopaminergic neurons for the formation of labile aversive memory', 'A dopamine-modulated neural circuit regulating aversive taste memory in Drosophila', and 'Three dopamine pathways induce aversive odor memories with different stability'. To find more information, you can query VFB for the dopaminergic PPL1 neuron or search for related publications.

results.question: Trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. What are the intermediate neuron types and their connections?
results.response:
To trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn, we can look at the intermediate neuron types and their connections. The pathway is described as: [olfactory receptor neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005926 "Open olfactory receptor neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") -> antennal lobe projection neuron -> lateral horn. 

VFB holds a range of data related to the [adult lateral horn](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007053 "Open adult lateral horn in Virtual Fly Brain"), including images, neurons with some part in the adult lateral horn, neurons with synaptic terminals, tracts/nerves innervating the adult lateral horn, lineage clones, images of neurons, and transgene expression. results.title: Anatomical containment chain
results.question: Trace the anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure. What is each level in the hierarchy?
results.response:
The containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure is as follows: 
DA1 glomerulus -> [antennal lobe glomerulus DA1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003932 "Open antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 in Virtual Fly Brain") -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum -> adult central brain -> adult brain. 
This information comes from the VFB database, which records the parent-child relationships between brain structures. 
VFB holds multiple records that describe this hierarchy, including the relationships between the adult antennal lobe and the adult deutocerebrum, adult cerebrum, and adult central brain, as well as the relationship between the adult central brain and the adult brain. 
To further explore this hierarchy, you can query the VFB database for the parent and child structures of each level in the hierarchy.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, as recorded in VFB. According to VFB, the giant fiber neuron has a unique anatomy and connectivity, with its large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum and a large descending axon that enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle and descends on the ipsilateral side in the dorsal cervical fasciculus. The neuron has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center. 

VFB holds [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of the giant fiber neuron, as well as data on [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") splits targeting it and [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") transgene expressions in it. The downstream connectivity classes for the giant fiber neuron are annotated in [389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records, while the upstream connectivity classes are annotated in [472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records.

The giant fiber neuron is mentioned in various publications, including those by Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), Namiki et al. (2018), and Power (1948), as cited in VFB. These publications provide further information on the anatomy, connectivity, and function of the giant fiber neuron. 

Available driver lines and further details on the giant fiber neuron can be explored through the splits and transgene expression data available in VFB.
